expectations.text: Uses a long enough comparison window that a single quiet interval does not fire the signal
expectations.evidence: For high, steady traffic, the design uses a short window (15–60 min) and a long window (hours to a day). It fires only when volume is below baseline in both, so one quiet short interval alone does not alert. The baseline is the same hour-of-week over the last 2–4 weeks. For low-volume traffic, it fires only when the gap exceeds the p99 of past gaps plus a margin. Its examples show this tolerance: a nightly sync becomes silent only after missing two nights, and a 40-minute gap on a 3-calls/hour integration does not count. expectations.text: Uses a long enough comparison window that a single quiet interval does not fire the signal
expectations.evidence: The answer addresses this in several places. The silence window is sized statistically per flow (T ≈ 9/λ, so a normal gap has about a 1e-4 chance). It has a 15-minute floor so jitter does not page, and it is benchmarked against a 4-week hour-of-week baseline. The partial-collapse detector also needs 3 consecutive windows below 20% before it fires. One gap remains: the silence alert itself fires once a single sized window is exceeded, with no consecutive-window requirement. Hysteresis applies only to resolving the alert, not to firing it. That keeps the score below 5.
